h: More for GS-1 — Society, History, Geography

items.d: **Census 2027 enumerates caste for the first time since 1931.** Consequences to name: the **50% ceiling** argument becomes empirical rather than notional; **sub-categorisation** (Rohini Commission, *Davinder Singh* 2024) gains data; welfare targeting sharpens; and the counter-risk is that enumeration **hardens identity** it merely meant to measure.

Inter-caste marriages remain roughly **5-6% of all marriages** (India Human Development Survey), which is why Ambedkar's diagnosis — caste survives through endogamy — is not a historical observation but a current one. **Shakti Vahini (2018)** on honour crimes is the legal anchor.

items.t: Urban anonymity has not dissolved caste
items.d: Residential segregation by caste persists in Indian cities, and matrimonial and rental markets remain caste-sorted — evidence against the assumption that urbanisation is automatically an emancipator. Use to complicate any 'modernisation ends caste' argument.

Adivasis are about **8.6% of the population** but a disproportionate share of those displaced by dams, mines and industry since 1947, with rehabilitation historically incomplete. **PESA (1996)**, the **FRA (2006)** and *Niyamgiri* (2013) exist because consent was the missing element.

Indian women perform roughly **7 times** the unpaid domestic and care work men do (Time Use Survey, 2019), and this — not preference or education — is the binding constraint on female labour force participation. The strongest single fact for a gender-and-economy answer.

Only about a quarter of India's elderly have any pension, and the **60-plus share doubles to ~20.8% by 2050**; **feminisation of ageing** means the typical poor elderly person is a widow with no independent income. Instruments: MWPSC Act 2007, Atal Vayo Abhyuday, and Ayushman Bharat's 70+ universal cover.

**Bipan Chandra's** distinction matters in an answer: communalism is the **ideology** (three stages — common secular interests, different interests, hostile interests); violence is only its episodic symptom. Remedies that address violence alone treat the symptom.

**Principled distance** (Bhargava): the state may intervene in religion to protect rights — temple entry, triple talaq, Sabarimala — and abstain otherwise. This is why Indian secularism looks 'interventionist' beside French laïcité and is not therefore less secular.

groups.g: History and culture — one more line each

items.d: **No common leadership, no shared aim, no coordination across regions, the south and Punjab largely uninvolved, superior British communications (telegraph and railway), and support from several princely states.** Six reasons, and the last two are the ones most answers miss.

Their achievement was **the economic critique** — Naoroji's drain theory, Ranade and Dutt — which built the intellectual case before the mass movement could be built. Dismissing them as petitioners misses that the extremists inherited an argument the moderates had already won.

He converted the Congress from an annual gathering of elites into a **mass organisation with a permanent structure** — linguistic provincial committees, a working committee, membership at four annas — after the Nagpur session (1920). The organisational change mattered as much as satyagraha.

**Sarojini Naidu** (Congress president, 1925), **Kasturba**, **Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay** (Dandi salt satyagraha, courted arrest), **Aruna Asaf Ali** (Quit India flag at Gowalia Tank), **Usha Mehta** (Congress Radio), **Rani Gaidinliu** (Naga resistance), **Matangini Hazra**, **Bhikaji Cama** (flag at Stuttgart, 1907). Names beat the generic sentence.

**10-12 million displaced, up to a million dead, and about 75,000 women abducted** — the largest forced migration in recorded history, effected across a line drawn in five weeks by a man who had never been to India. The abduction figure is the one most answers omit.

**Junagadh** (ruler acceded to Pakistan, plebiscite went to India), **Hyderabad** (Operation Polo, 1948), **Kashmir** (Instrument of Accession, 26 October 1947). Naming what made each different is the answer; 'Patel integrated 565 states' is the preamble.

South Indian temples were **landholders, employers, bankers and irrigation managers** — Chola inscriptions record endowments, interest rates and grain measures. This converts a culture answer into a political-economy one, which is where the marks are.

**Muziris, Barygaza (Bharuch), Arikamedu, Tamralipti** traded with Rome, Arabia and Southeast Asia; the *Periplus of the Erythraean Sea* is the source. The point: the Indian Ocean was a **connected commercial world long before European arrival**, which reframes 'the age of discovery'.

groups.g: Geography — the mechanisms most often confused

items.t: Why the Bay gets more cyclones
items.d: Higher sea surface temperature, **freshwater influx from the Ganga-Brahmaputra stratifying the surface and keeping it warm**, proximity to the monsoon trough, and slower dissipation over the shallow shelf — while the Arabian Sea is drier and cooler, though warming is narrowing the gap. Four mechanisms, not one.

items.t: Why Tamil Nadu is dry in the south-west monsoon
items.d: It lies in the **rain shadow of the Western Ghats** during June-September and receives its main rainfall from the **retreating north-east monsoon (Oct-Dec)**, when the winds have picked up moisture crossing the Bay. The clearest example of aspect determining a rainfall regime.

The **Narmada and Tapi form estuaries** because they flow through **rift valleys** with steep gradients and little sediment load reaching a subsiding coast, while the Ganga, Godavari and Krishna build deltas on a gentle, aggrading shelf. Structure, not size, decides.

items.t: Western Disturbances matter more than they look
items.d: Extratropical cyclones from the Mediterranean, steered by the **sub-tropical westerly jet**, delivering the **winter rain the rabi wheat crop depends on** and the snow that feeds the Himalayan rivers in summer. Their weakening or shift is a food-security question, not just a weather one.

items.t: Groundwater as the real irrigation system
items.d: Groundwater supplies about **60% of irrigation and 85% of rural drinking water**, extraction stage ~60%, with over-exploited blocks concentrated in **Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and western UP** — the same states where power is free and procurement assured. The map of depletion is the map of the incentive.

items.t: Laterite, and why it matters economically
items.d: Formed by **heavy rain, high temperature and leaching** that strips silica and leaves iron and aluminium — poor in humus and nitrogen, so agriculturally weak, but the source of **bauxite** and a traditional building brick. Links a soil type to a mineral answer.
